configuration: Fourteen of the seventeen upstream cases of unittest/joint-configurations.cpp on upstream's buildModelWithAllJoints, a twelve-joint model with nq 30 and nv 27. The model's topology and joint types are upstream's, reproduced in the adapter; the body inertia and three limit vectors of each joint, which upstream draws from the unseeded stream, and every operand of every case are read from ic/<ic>/operands.json.
observable: the configuration-space operations of a whole robot: integrate, difference, interpolate, distance and its per-joint squared form, neutral, normalize, the derivatives of integrate and difference in every assignment mode, the parallel transport of a Jacobian, the tangent map in its four equivalent forms and the coefficient-wise integrate Jacobian
default_vs_upstream: upstream, except that the model numbers and the operands are frozen rather than drawn, and integrateCoeffWiseJacobian_test runs on the same twelve-joint model rather than on a second, humanoid one
variant: Two units in the last place, toward positive infinity, on every nonzero component of every frozen item in ic/nominal/operands.json. Perturbing every component rather than one was measured, not assumed: with a single component per item, 18 of cpp-explog's 48 observables and 6 of cpp-spatial's 76 came back with a spread of exactly zero, because a relative change of 2.2e-16 in one entry of a rotation matrix rounds away in the last bit of an output built from all nine. Every component still moves by exactly two units in the last place, so this stays the generic two-ulp noise calibration rather than a physics experiment. A component that is exactly zero is never perturbed, because two ulps above zero is a subnormal, which is a meaningless perturbation of a physical quantity and a parser hazard besides. The worst measured spread is 1.5543e-15 absolute. 12 of the 45 observables show a spread of exactly zero and are insensitive by construction, not by accident. They are the cases upstream runs at a constructed configuration rather than at a drawn one: the all-ones configuration, the neutral configuration, and the configuration one unit of every degree of freedom away from neutral. No operand reaches them, by upstream's construction, and freezing does not change that. Their bound therefore rests on the physical argument in the warrant rather than on a measured sensitivity, and a reviewer should read it that way.
altbuild: none: the same official.cpp compiled at -O0 with -ffp-contract=off against the same pinned source reproduces the -O2 result bit-identically for every graded value of this check, so an alternative build measures a floor of exactly zero and supplies no evidence. Eigen fixes the evaluation order of these expressions and the arithmetic is scalar, so the compiler has nothing to reassociate.

evidence.floor_how: The same official.cpp compiled twice against the same pinned source, once at -O2 -DNDEBUG and once at -O0 -ffp-contract=off, and run on ic/nominal; every graded value was bit-identical, so the measured floor is 0.0 and the bound is set from the variant spread and the physics instead. The probe was repeated on the worker on 2026-09-14 (x86_64, inside the env image); the result was unchanged, bit-identical.

warrant: The graded quantities are the configuration-space operations of a whole robot: integrate, difference, interpolate, distance and its per-joint squared form, neutral, normalize, the derivatives of integrate and difference in every assignment mode, the parallel transport of a Jacobian, the tangent map in its four equivalent forms and the coefficient-wise integrate Jacobian, in SI units and in the coordinate order the joint model, the Lie group or the spatial type fixes, which is part of the input and not something an implementation chooses. The bound is 1e-09 absolute plus 1e-11 relative, so on the largest graded magnitude here, about 9.36e+00, it admits about 1.09e-09. It is physical because every implementation fault this test can express is many orders of magnitude larger: a transposed motion subspace, a rotation composed in the wrong order, a dropped Taylor branch near the identity, a sign error in a cross product or a missing scaling on a mimic joint each move individual values by between 1e-2 and 1e+2 in these units, seven to eleven decades above the bound, and a relative error of one part in a thousand injected into the largest graded value of this check lands 8,557,443 times over it. Every upstream identity also stays active, so such a fault is rejected twice over. It is achievable because a correct port that reassociates these expressions differs by about n eps |x|, roughly 30 * 2.2e-16 * 9.36e+00, which is decades inside the bound. Measured on this host: the two-ulp variant moves the worst of the 22,205 graded values by 1.5543e-15, using 1.530e-06 of the bound, that is 653,533 times of headroom, and the alternative build measured exactly zero. The bound is loose enough for a genuinely different implementation on another device and tight enough that no fault the upstream test is written to catch could pass it.
